description: The World Database on Protected Areas is the most complete global source of information on protected areas, holding spatial and tabular data on more than 200,000 sites, about 91 percent as polygon boundaries and the rest as points. Attributes include the WDPA identifier, name in English and the original language, designation and its level (national, regional such as Natura 2000 or OSPAR, international such as Ramsar and World Heritage), IUCN management category, reported area, status and governance. It is managed by UNEP-WCMC with support from IUCN and WCPA and compiled from submissions by governments, NGOs, landowners and communities. Coverage is worldwide, land and marine, updated monthly, with monthly versions archived since July 2017 in the Earth Engine copy. Data are available on Protected Planet and as Earth Engine feature collections; they are free for non-commercial use, and any commercial use of the data or derivatives needs prior written permission from UNEP-WCMC. Caveats: completeness and boundary accuracy depend on national submissions, some countries restrict sharing, and point-only sites have no extent. It is a reference layer for green and blue infrastructure, environmental constraints on infrastructure siting and ecosystem-based adaptation; related records are the Global Mangrove Watch, the Allen Coral Atlas, GLWD and ESA WorldCover.
